records.label: spacr.channel_sorting#3
records.source: 1. **Channels and sets.** Each image gets a CHANNEL, and images that show the same field in different channels share a SET. Channels come from the user's selection (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) or from a regex's ``chanID`` group; sets come from the regex's other named groups (:func:`parse_names`, checked by :func:`check_sets`), from a regex spaCR proposes (:func:`infer_regex`), or, ignoring names, from pairing each image with the most similar image of the same size in every other channel (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **The plan.** :func:`build_plan` names every set in the Yokogawa / CellVoyager form ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- exactly what ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` parses -- and lists every move. It writes nothing. 3. **Apply.** :func:`apply_plan` moves each image into ``C01/``, ``C02/``... under a new folder, its mask into that channel folder's ``masks/`` under the new name (and its ``.curation.json`` ledger with it, so the pairing survives), records every move in ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv``, and then :func:`merge_sorted` builds ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` and ``merged/`` with spaCR's own functions (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` and :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), so each merged array has the pipeline's own layout: intensity channels first, then one label plane per mask role in the order cell, nucleus, pathogen.
records.context: 1. **Image data channels and sets.** Each image gets an image data channel, and images that show the same microscope field of view in different image data channels share a SET. image data channels come from the user's selection (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) or from a regex's ``chanID`` group; sets come from the regex's other named groups (:func:`parse_names`, checked by :func:`check_sets`), from a regex spaCR proposes (:func:`infer_regex`), or, ignoring names, from pairing each image with the most similar image of the same size in every other image data channel (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **The plan.** :func:`build_plan` names every set in the Yokogawa / CellVoyager form ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- exactly what ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` parses -- and lists every move. It writes nothing. 3. **Apply.** :func:`apply_plan` moves each image into ``C01/``, ``C02/``... under a new folder, its mask into that image data channel folder's ``masks/`` under the new name (and its ``.curation.json`` ledger with it, so the pairing survives), records every move in ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv``, and then :func:`merge_sorted` builds ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` and ``merged/`` with spaCR's own functions (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` and :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), so each merged array has the workflow's own layout: intensity image data channels first, then one label image layer per mask role in the order cell, nucleus, pathogen.
records.translation: 1. **Kanäle und Sätze.** Jedes Bild erhält einen KANAL, und Bilder, die dasselbe Sichtfeld in verschiedenen Kanälen zeigen, teilen sich einen SATZ. Kanäle stammen aus der Auswahl des Benutzers (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) oder aus der Gruppe ``chanID`` eines regulären Ausdrucks; Sätze stammen aus den übrigen benannten Gruppen des regulären Ausdrucks (:func:`parse_names`, geprüft von :func:`check_sets`), aus einem regulären Ausdruck, den spaCR vorschlägt (:func:`infer_regex`), oder, ohne Rücksicht auf Namen, aus der Paarung jedes Bildes mit dem ähnlichsten gleich großen Bild in jedem anderen Kanal (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **Der Plan.** :func:`build_plan` benennt jeden Satz in der Yokogawa/CellVoyager-Form ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- genau das, was ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` einliest -- und listet jede Verschiebung auf. Er schreibt nichts. 3. **Anwenden.** :func:`apply_plan` verschiebt jedes Bild nach ``C01/``, ``C02/``... unter einem neuen Ordner, seine Maske in das ``masks/`` dieses Kanalordners unter dem neuen Namen (und sein Protokoll ``.curation.json`` mit ihr, damit die Zuordnung erhalten bleibt), hält jede Verschiebung in ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv`` fest, und dann baut :func:`merge_sorted` ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` und ``merged/`` mit den eigenen Funktionen von spaCR (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` und :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), sodass jedes zusammengeführte Array die eigene Struktur der Pipeline hat: zuerst die Intensitätskanäle, dann eine Label-Ebene pro Maskenrolle in der Reihenfolge Zelle, Kern, Pathogen.

records.source: Regex conventions: ``chanID`` is the channel; ``plateID``, ``wellID``, ``fieldID`` and ``timeID`` say where a set goes; any other named group only helps tell sets apart. records.source: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the channel -- or, when the user assigned channels, the tokens that only follow the channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per channel. Of the candidates that pass, the one with the FEWEST channels wins: any name can be read as a channel of its own in a single set, which passes and means nothing.
records.context: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the image data channel -- or, when the user assigned image data channels, the tokens that only follow the image data channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per image data channel. Each candidate is checked with :func:`check_sets` before it is returned. spaCR's own Yokogawa pattern is tried first, and :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` last. Of the candidates that pass, the one with the FEWEST image data channels wins: any name can be read as an image data channel of its own in a single set, which passes and means nothing.
records.translation: Namen werden in Token zerlegt (an ``_ - . space`` und, falls das nicht geht, in Ziffern- und Buchstabenfolgen); die veränderlichen Token werden ermittelt; eines wird als Kanal versucht -- oder, wenn der Benutzer Kanäle zugewiesen hat, werden die Token, die nur dem Kanal folgen, beiseitegelegt --, und der Rest muss einen Satz identifizieren, der genau ein Bild pro Kanal enthält. Jeder Kandidat wird mit :func:`check_sets` geprüft, bevor er zurückgegeben wird. Das eigene Yokogawa-Muster von spaCR wird zuerst versucht und :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` zuletzt. Von den bestandenen Kandidaten gewinnt der mit den WENIGSTEN Kanälen: Jeder Name lässt sich als eigener Kanal in einem einzigen Satz lesen, was besteht und nichts bedeutet.
